text: Setting clear goals is essential for any project's success. One effective method is to use SMART goals, which means they are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," you might set a goal to "increase user sign-ups by 15% within three months." Once your main goals are defined, break them into smaller milestones. These are checkpoints that help you track progress and stay motivated. Each milestone should lead to a deliverable, such as a completed report or a working prototype. Finally, ensure all stakeholders agree on the objectives. When everyone—from team members to clients—has aligned expectations, communication flows more smoothly, and the project is far more likely to succeed.
